summary: Ustaz Azlan discusses the hidden ten years of the Prophet's SAW life after marrying Khadijah, then tells how the Kaaba was rebuilt when he was 35: why it was fragile, the pure funds, the stone and architect Bakum from a Roman ship, the dispute over placing the Black Stone, and how the Prophet SAW united the tribes with a cloth. The ustaz also explains the hadith on the Black Stone, Umar's words, and changes to the Kaaba's design including the Hijr Ismail.
keyPoints: Little is recorded of the ten years after the marriage to Khadijah, yet the Prophet SAW supported a large household and grew the business.
The Kaaba was rebuilt because of floods, fire and theft, using funds from pure sources only.
The tribes competed for the honour of placing the Black Stone until blood was nearly shed.
The Prophet SAW, known as Al-Amin, solved the dispute by spreading a cloth and having every tribe hold it.
The Black Stone is only a stone; kissing it by the sunnah must never lead to harming others.
The Prophet SAW wished to rebuild the Kaaba on Ibrahim's foundations but postponed it because his people had only just accepted Islam.

chapters.title: Opening and the floods
chapters.summary: The ustaz prays for flood victims and recaps the story of the two Zayds.

chapters.title: The hidden ten years after the marriage
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW built his family and business and supported the household and Makkah's poor.

chapters.title: The Prophet's SAW sons and 'cut off'
chapters.summary: His sons died young, yet his name continues to be raised high.

chapters.title: Background to the Kaaba's construction
chapters.summary: Views on who first built it, and two thousand years of damage and repair.

chapters.title: Floods, fire and theft
chapters.summary: The Kaaba was weakened by valley floods, fire and its low door, and theft pushed Quraysh to rebuild.

chapters.title: Pure funds for the project
chapters.summary: Quraysh accepted only clean money; the ustaz links this to purifying non-shariah-compliant funds.

chapters.title: The Roman ship and the architect Bakum
chapters.summary: A Roman ship ran aground at Jeddah and its materials and architect were bought.

chapters.title: Al-Walid begins the demolition
chapters.summary: Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah started the demolition after everyone feared punishment.

chapters.title: The report of loosening the cloth
chapters.summary: The ustaz doubts that the report of the loincloth fits the age of 35.

chapters.title: The dispute over placing the Black Stone
chapters.summary: Construction halted for five days and tribes dipped their hands in blood.

chapters.title: Al-Amin solves the problem
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW was the first man through the gate and placed the stone on a cloth.

chapters.title: The Black Stone and its hadith
chapters.summary: Its origin in Paradise, its darkening by sin, and its witnessing on the Day of Judgement.

chapters.title: Etiquette and Umar's words
chapters.summary: Kissing is not obligatory; Umar said it is only a stone; and the stone's history.

chapters.title: The Kaaba's new design and lessons
chapters.summary: The Hijr Ismail, high door, roof and gutter; Aisha's hadith; and that taqwa cannot be measured.

people.role: A seeker of tawhid before prophethood
people.context: Robbed and killed on his way home, five years before the Prophet SAW was sent.
Would later support the Prophet SAW at the time of revelation, built on a firm ten-year bond.
Died as a newborn and was greeted with taunts of 'cut off' from the Prophet's SAW uncles.
An example that people could enter the Kaaba because its door was low.
Sent to build a church in Yemen but hired to rebuild the Kaaba.
First to demolish a wall of the Kaaba after praying.
In the loincloth report, told the Prophet SAW to do the same.
Proposed that the first man through the Safa gate decide the dispute.
Told the Black Stone that it is only a stone.
Heard the Prophet SAW express a wish to rebuild the Kaaba on Ibrahim's foundations.
His adhan from the Kaaba after the Conquest shows no difference of colour or background.

lessons.title: Praying for disaster victims
lessons.body: The ustaz opens with a prayer for flood victims in several states.

lessons.title: The husband provides
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW supported the family, not Khadijah, including stepchildren and adopted children.

lessons.title: The Prophet's SAW name is not cut off
lessons.body: Though no son survived, his name is raised high until the Day of Judgement.

lessons.title: Rebuilding needs pure funds
lessons.body: Quraysh refused haram money; impure funds can be purified but not for mosques.

lessons.title: Allah's planning behind events
lessons.body: A ship carrying church materials was stranded and its cargo used for the Kaaba.

lessons.title: Trust earns a name
lessons.body: Every tribe called him Al-Amin at once.

lessons.title: An inclusive solution
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW spread a cloth so every tribe took part and no one was left out.

lessons.title: The Black Stone is only a stone
lessons.body: There is no need to push or harm others to kiss it; one can gesture with the hand.

lessons.title: Beware scams around the Kaaba
lessons.body: Watch for people who offer to take you to kiss the Black Stone for a fee.

lessons.title: Change in stages
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW postponed rebuilding the Kaaba because his people had only just accepted Islam.

lessons.title: People cannot measure taqwa
lessons.body: Only Allah knows taqwa; measuring it by a donation box or appearance is wrong.

lessons.title: No idols inside the Kaaba
lessons.body: The interior is empty apart from pillars, not a place for idols.

glossary.meaning: The black stone at the corner of the Kaaba, the starting point of tawaf.
The semicircular walled area beside the Kaaba; praying in it counts as praying inside the Kaaba.
The most trustworthy, the Prophet's SAW title before prophethood.
The area between the Black Stone and the Kaaba's door, a place where du'a is answered.
Restoration, distinct from rebuilding, which demolishes and builds again.
The phrase 'he has been cut off' thrown at the Prophet SAW when his son died.

dalil.context: Ibrahim's du'a 'I settled by Your House' shows the site already bore traces before the rebuilding. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Our Lord, I have established some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley, close to Your Sacred House, Lord, so that they may keep up the prayer. Make people’s hearts turn to them, and provide them with produce, so that they may be thankful.

dalil.context: Allah tells in the Quran that Ibrahim and Ismail built the Kaaba. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: As Abraham and Ishmael built up the foundations of the House [they prayed], ‘Our Lord, accept [this] from us. You are the All Hearing, the All Knowing.

dalil.context: Explains the origin and colour of the Black Stone.
dalil.translation: The Black Stone came down from Paradise, whiter than milk, and turned black from the sins of the children of Adam.

dalil.context: The ustaz notes scholars differ on how strong the added phrase about the polytheists' sins is.
dalil.translation: The Black Stone came down from Paradise whiter than snow, and became black from the sins of the polytheists.

dalil.context: A hadith on the stone's status on the Day of Judgement.
dalil.translation: By Allah, Allah will raise the stone on the Day of Judgement with two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, testifying for whoever touched it.

dalil.context: Shows that the stone is only a stone and kissing it is following the sunnah.
dalil.translation: I know you are only a stone that neither harms nor benefits; had I not seen the Prophet SAW kiss you, I would not kiss you.

dalil.context: Major change must be made in stages.
dalil.translation: Were your people not recently converted to Islam, I would demolish the Kaaba and rebuild it to Ibrahim's true dimensions.
